title: Time value of money and financial maths
objectives: Compute FV, PV, annuity and EMI-style problems.
Use real return and the rule of 72.
body_md:
## Core formulas

- **FV = PV × (1 + r)^n**; **PV = FV ÷ (1 + r)^n**.
- **Annuity FV** (SIP, end of period): P × [((1 + r)^n − 1) ÷ r].
- **EMI** = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1) (r per period).
- **Rule of 72:** doubling time ≈ 72 ÷ rate %.
- **Real return** = (1 + nominal) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1.
- **Effective annual rate** = (1 + r/m)^m − 1.

## Examples

| Problem | Answer |
|---|---|
| ₹1 lakh at 10% for 3 years | ₹1.331 lakh |
| ₹12 lakh needed in 5 years at 10% (lump sum today) | PV = 12 ÷ 1.6105 ≈ ₹7.45 lakh |
| Real return at 10% nominal, 6% inflation | 1.10 ÷ 1.06 − 1 ≈ 3.8% |

## Goal funding

Inflate the goal cost to the goal date, then compute the required lump sum or monthly SIP.

> **Exam tip:** Do the inflation step first; the number must be in future rupees.
example: A degree costs ₹20 lakh today and education inflation is 8%. In 10 years it costs 20 × 1.08^10 ≈ ₹43.2 lakh. The SIP needed is computed against that number.
say: Your goal is ₹43 lakh in future rupees, not ₹20 lakh.
At this return, the monthly SIP required is shown here.
never: Return is guaranteed, so plan to the rupee.
